brief: BTIG's technical strategist flags a key reversal day in 30yr Treasury yields: an overnight marginal new high gave way to a close below the prior day's lows, following yesterday's note that yields showed upside exhaustion and a tactical pullback over coming weeks would not surprise. He does not call this the end of the yield up-cycle, but says tactical risk/reward has turned firmly against higher yields. A sentiment signal reinforces this: a widely read publication's "Will bonds blow up?" cover, from a title with a history of running covers late in a move as a contrarian indicator. On what a yield pullback means for stocks, he pushes back on the consensus bullish read: lower yields plausibly helps small-caps (IWM) and equal-weight (RSP), which were hurt by the yield surge, but it is curious semis or QQQ would benefit when they were immune to rising rates. His pain trade is therefore lower rates alongside lower SMH, QQQ and XLK. Separately, the RTY/NDX ratio sits at its 8th-lowest RSI reading since 1985; a yield reversion should support that ratio, but direction is unclear. RTY is down ~10% into its 200-day average, a setup that usually bounces, but he has more conviction NDX moves lower than that many would expect during a bond rally.
